questions: Have your eyes appeared more prominent or “bulging” recently?
Did this change begin suddenly or worsen rapidly?
Do you have decreased or blurred vision in either eye?
Do you have eye pain, pain with eye movement, or severe headache?
Is either eye red, swollen, or difficult to close completely?
Have you had fever, recent sinus infection, or an injury around the eye?
Have you noticed unequal pupils or new drooping of an eyelid?
Have you been diagnosed with thyroid disease or had symptoms such as weight loss, tremor, palpitations, or heat intolerance?
Have you had similar eye problems before?

results: 1. Bedside neuro-ophthalmic examination, including visual acuity, visual fields, pupillary responses, ocular alignment, and extraocular movements
cranial nerve examination: bilateral ophthalmoparesis with severe limitation of extraocular movements and right exotropia; ptosis improved
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
2. Ice-pack test with assessment for improvement in ptosis and diplopia
ice-pack test: POSITIVE
3. Urgent CT angiography of the head and neck
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
4. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast
MRI orbits: SEVERE THINNING of all extraocular muscles; exotropia of the right eye
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
5. Serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: acetylcholine receptor antibodies strongly positive, 10.32 nmol/L
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: 10.32 nmol/L (normal <0.50) - strongly POSITIVE
6. Serum MuSK antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: acetylcholine receptor antibodies strongly positive, 10.32 nmol/L
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
7. Repetitive nerve stimulation and/or single-fiber electromyography of facial and extraocular muscles
repetitive nerve stimulation: decremental response
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti–acetylcholine receptor antibody–positive ocular myasthenia gravis causing bilateral ophthalmoparesis, ptosis, and secondary extraocular-muscle atrophy

ALTERNATIVE 1: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia due to a mitochondrial myopathy

ALTERNATIVE 2: Thyroid-associated orbitopathy

ALTERNATIVE 3: Miller–Fisher syndrome (acute ophthalmoplegia variant of Guillain–Barré syndrome)
